cands.bio: Retired U.S. Army officer (2004–2024) and preacher from Carrollton, Alabama. Served as a congressional fellow for Rep. Robert Aderholt and as human capital director at the White House National Security Council. Holds an MBA and a master's in legislative affairs. Has never held elected office.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as endorsed by the West Alabama voter group Sway (Erin TheCoOpGal).

cands.gaps: We found no statements or actions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or foreign land buyers, growth and land conservation, H-1B or immigration enforcement, abortion, or school vouchers and teacher pay. His survey answers mention school funding, gun laws that honor Second Amendment rights, law enforcement, rural hospitals and veterans only in general terms, so they could not be matched to specific positions. We found no record of any elected office, so there is no voting record. We found no news coverage of controversies. We could not confirm when he lived in Alabama as an adult, since his military and Washington, D.C. postings are not dated by place. We also found no information on his endorsements beyond one small voter-group listing.

cands.bio: Republican state senator for Alabama Senate District 21 since 2010. He served in the Alabama House (District 62) from 1994 to 2010. A University of Alabama graduate (1973), he owns CASHCO Marketing and has worked as a Tuscaloosa County parks athletic director and school coach.

endorsements.text: In 2010 his endorsements included the Alabama Tea Party Express.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions by Gerald Allen on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land purchases, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, policing and pensions, or school choice and teacher pay. We found only 2010 and 2014 campaign-website statements on guns and abortion, and nothing from the 2026 campaign. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. Where he grew up is not stated in the pages we had. Ballotpedia found no endorsements for 2026, and its list of bills he sponsored was empty.
